topic: Compile-Time vs. Runtime Polymorphism and the Impact on Memory Layout and Performance
explanation: This focuses on the difference between static polymorphism (achieved through function overloading and templates) and dynamic polymorphism (achieved through virtual functions and inheritance).  We'll examine how compilers implement these, their impact on memory layout (e.g., virtual function tables (vtables)), and performance implications (e.g., function call overhead, branching, and memory access patterns).  Static polymorphism often leads to better performance due to compile-time resolution, while dynamic polymorphism offers flexibility but incurs runtime overhead.
